newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola ends down on commission, hedge sales.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola ends down on commission, hedge sales.

text.p: WCE canola ended lower Thursday on commission house and hedge selling, traders said.

"There were light hedges at the close, commission houses sold and UGG was a featured buyer of the January," a trader said. March-July spread at $0.50, Jan-March $0.40, Jan-May $1. More than 800 contracts traded on bull spreading, traders said. Estimated volume was 3,605 lots with 200 hedges.

January canola ended $0.50 down at $404.50 a tonne, March fell $1.10 to $404.60. January flax rose $0.50 to $364.70 on commercial short covering of old export business met by light hedges, traders said.
February western barley rose $0.90 to $139.70, March rose $0.30 to $139.20 on commercial demand as Midland Walwyn sold. Feb-Mar and Mar-May spread at even money. Volume was 1,000.
December feed wheat lost $0.20 to $172.50 on commission, local selling, March fell $0.10 to $174.40. Dec-Mar spread at $1.50. Estimated volume was light at 300 lots.
Benson Quinn sold 25 December oats unchanged at US$121 to a commercial. Commercials bought three December feed peas up US$1.50 to US$207.50, traders said.
U.S. markets were closed for U.S. Thanksgiving.
(All values in Canadian dollars except peas, oats).
